MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of marine and freshwater environments? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of marine and freshwater environments.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Fish culture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Fish culture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Fish culture.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Fish culture.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Fish culture.

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture? (1 mark)

   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovations in aquaculture.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Technologies and Innovation in Aquaculture 3.0 Capture Fisheries 3.1 Conservatio.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

14. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond? (1 mark)

   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conservation of Marine and Freshwater Environments 3.2 Weather and Climatic Cond.

   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity

   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
